{{Short description|American taxonomist}}
'''John Paget Figg-Hoblyn''' Ph.D ([[Biological science]]) (January 25, 1926 – June 12, 2011){{cn|date=November 2020}} was a university professor, and [[taxonomist]]. He came to public attention when a [[BBC]] documentary was broadcast about the search for him in 1994, after he had failed to claim an inheritance which included [[Fir Hill Manor]].

==Inheritance dispute==
Figg-Hoblyn came to public attention in 1994, when the [[BBC]] broadcast a documentary about him.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ftvdb.bfi.org.uk/sift/title/519699|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120406182215/http://ftvdb.bfi.org.uk/sift/title/519699|url-status=dead|archive-date=6 April 2012|title= The Curse of Fir Hill Manor|publisher=British Film Institute|accessdate=6 May 2013}}</ref><ref name="BBC mystery over heir">{{cite news|title=Mystery over heir to £5m fortune|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/cornwall/6394539.stm|newspaper=BBC News|date=25 February 2007}}</ref> In 1965 his father had bequeathed him a 1000-[[acre]] [[Estate (land)|estate]] and the ruins of a [[manor house]], [[Fir Hill Manor]], in [[Cornwall]], England. According to the [[Official Solicitor]], he failed to take up the inheritance.<ref name="BBC mystery over heir" /> The Official Solicitor was appointed in 1972 to manage the estate for John Figg-Hoblyn in the 1970s when they lost contact with him.<ref name="BBC mystery over heir" />

The BBC documentary discovered Figg-Hoblyn was living in a caravan park in [[California]], United States,<ref name="BBC mystery over heir" /> where he and his sister, Peggy, were following a low-key lifestyle trading in [[Organic food|organic produce]]. The BBC subsequently lost contact with him.<ref name="BBC mystery over heir" />

In 2007, the next-in-line to inherit the estate as the eldest male, John Westropp Figg-Hoblyn, put out a call to find John Paget Figg-Hoblyn before the inheritance which included [[Fir Hill Manor]] was lost.<ref name="BBC mystery over heir" /><ref name="Telegraph 2007">[https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/1543450/Heir-refuses-to-claim-5m-estate.html Heir refuses to claim £5m estate], ''Daily Telegraph'', 22 February 2007. Retrieved 6 May 2013.</ref>

John Paget Figg-Hoblyn died in a nursing home on 12 June 2011 at the age of 85.{{Where|date=March 2024}}{{cn|date=November 2020}}

==Academic career==
Figg-Hoblyn was educated at [[Stanford University]], [[California]], United States. In 1953, he described a unique species of [[jewel beetle]] that he had discovered, which was given the name ''Acmaeodera nanbrownae''. This name is now classified as a [[synonym (taxonomy)|junior synonym]] for ''Acmaeodera vanduzeei''.<ref>{{cite web|title=ITIS Standard Report Page: ''Acmaeodera nanbrownae''|url=https://www.itis.gov/servlet/SingleRpt/SingleRpt?search_topic=TSN&search_value=809609|work=Integrated Taxonomic Information System|accessdate=24 April 2013}}</ref> Dr. Figg-Hoblyn used to have a lab at Stanford University,{{citation needed|reason=This statement needs a citation to a source that supports it.|date=April 2013 }} and taught at San Jose State University.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bizarre family saga reaches a settlement|url=http://www.thisiscornwall.co.uk/Bizarre-family-saga-reaches-settlement/story-18400821-detail/story.html#ixzz2NXWRj6Hy|accessdate=24 April 2013|newspaper=Cornish Guardian|date=13 March 2013}}</ref>
